title: Case Study: Graph-based Matching & Recommendation
interviewAnswer: Explain why the problem is naturally a graph, how semantic PR features enter the graph, why an inductive GNN helps new PRs, how link prediction/ranking is evaluated and how popularity bias is handled.
why: This case demonstrates a general graph-based matching system that combines content semantics, interaction structure, candidate generation, ranking and bias controls.
intuition: Represent entities and interactions as a graph, encode content features, learn embeddings that capture both semantics and behavior, generate a manageable candidate set and then rank under product constraints.
deepDive: Graph-based matching is useful when historical interactions carry signal that tabular features alone miss. Node features can come from text/image encoders, graph message passing propagates neighborhood context, and a link-prediction or ranking decoder scores potential matches. Evaluation should reflect the serving task—Recall@K or NDCG rather than only AUC. Temporal splits, hard-negative sampling, cold-start handling, popularity bias, freshness and eligibility constraints are central production concerns.
workedExample: Represent users and opportunities/items as nodes, encode content features, learn graph embeddings from historical interactions, generate candidates, correct popularity bias and rank the top matches under availability and policy constraints.
commonMistakes: Using random edge splits that leak future interactions.
Optimizing AUC while production returns only top-K matches.
Ignoring cold-start entities and popularity/exposure bias.
followUps: Why use a graph instead of only content embeddings?
How would you create negative samples?
How would you handle unseen users/items?
How would you separate candidate generation from ranking?
production: Refresh graph edges/features incrementally, maintain a fast candidate stage, apply ranking and eligibility/business constraints, cache stable embeddings, monitor concentration/cold-start quality/latency and log exposure plus outcomes for retraining.
